meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the Committee discussed a matter submitted by a private party requesting the Committee to assess how effectively the regulations and guidelines made under Law No. 2/2024 (Occupational Health and Safety Act) are being implemented. Following deliberations, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed that a response be sent to the individual incorporating the information received from the Ministry of Higher Education, Labor and Skills Development. The proposal was seconded by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. The Committee also decided to urge the Ministry to finalize the guidelines and policies mandated under Section 73 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act. Next, the Committee discussed an issue submitted by North Galolhu Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim regarding the operation of harbors servicing international vessels. Following deliberations, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed that a response be sent to the petitioner incorporating the information received from the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation. The proposal was seconded by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. Lastly, the Committee discussed a matter submitted by North Galolhu Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim requesting clarification regarding the fire incident that occurred on 12 March 2026 at an accommodation block in Adh. Dhigurah, in which five expatriate workers lost their lives. When the floor was opened for discussion, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed that letters be sent to the relevant authorities to obtain further information on the matter. This proposal was seconded by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.)

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: The first item on the agenda was the election of a Chairperson to preside over the Committee pursuant to Article 163 of the Standing Orders of the 20th Majlis, as both the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson were unable to attend the meeting. The election process was presided over by Assistant Director General of Accounts, Niusa Ahmed Naseer. When the floor was opened for nominations, Dhangethi Constituency Member Abdulla Rasheed nominated Ali Fazad for the position of Chairperson. The nomination was seconded by South Hulhumale’ Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. Next, the Committee reviewed the request submitted by the President for parliamentary approval of the 12 Ministers appointed on 14 April 2026 and the 2 Ministers appointed on 15 April 2026, pursuant to Article 129(a) of the Constitution. When the floor was opened for discussion on how to proceed with the two matters, Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed proposed that both matters be considered and decided together. The proposal was seconded by Dhangethi Constituency Member Abdulla Rasheed. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. As it had been decided to consider the two matters together, Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed proposed to approve the appointments of all 14 Ministers appointed by the President on 14 and 15 April 2026. The proposal was seconded by Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. (Voting details are provided in the “Votes” section of this page.)

meetings.title: 9th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the Committee discussed a matter submitted by a private party requesting the Committee to assess how effectively the regulations and guidelines made under Law No. 2/2024 (Occupational Health and Safety Act) are being implemented. Following a discussion on the response received from the Ministry of Higher Education, Labour, and Skills Development, it was noted that only one regulation has been published under the Act to date. Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazad proposed that a letter be sent to the Attorney General’s Office seeking clarification on the reasons for the delay in issuing the remaining regulations. This proposal was seconded by West Henveyru Member Ali Ibrahim. The proposal was passed unanimously. Next, the committee discussed a matter submitted by North Galolhu Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim, seeking some clarifications from Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation and Maldives Ports Limited regarding the operation of ports that service international vessels. Accordingly, it was decided to proceed with this matter after obtaining further information related to the case from the relevant authorities. Lastly, during the opportunity opened for committee members to propose issues they wished to raise, Hulhumalé Central Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed that due to complaints being received that the salaries and benefits of employees in some sectors have decreased following the changes to the "State Pay Framework," a meeting should be held with officials from the National Pay Commission to clarify the matter. This proposal was seconded by Central Fuvahmulah Member Ali Fazad. The proposal was passed unanimously. Details of votes taken in this meeting are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 6th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The first thing that was discussed in today's meeting was the issue regarding healthcare workers’ overtime payment policies. When the floor was opened, South Hulhumale Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed to make a decision on this matter only after the Joint Committee comprising the Committee on National Development and Heritage and the Committee on Social Affairs is done reviewing “Resolution to find out the views of MPs on the rules for paying overtime work by education workers and health workers and establishing a fair work environment for them.” This proposal was seconded by South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain. The proposal was passed unanimously. Secondly, the committee discussed issues related to the Health Services Act (Law No.29/2015) and the Healthcare Professionals Act (Law No. 13/2015), as well as the challenges in accessing commonly used medications. When the floor was opened, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed that both matters be referred to the Committee on Social Affairs, as they fall under its mandate. This proposal was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The proposal was passed unanimously. Thirdly, the Committee proceeded with examining the matter regarding F. Magoodhoo Airport, where despite 85% of the construction work being completed and having the necessary materials and personnel available, work has been halted. Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed to send a letter to the relevant ministry to clarify the date when work can resume, and the estimated date for the airport's opening. This proposal was seconded by South Hulhumale Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed. The proposal was passed unanimously. Lastly, the Committee reviewed a letter sent by a private individual, outlining the difficulties faced in obtaining assistance from the National Social Protection Agency (NSPA) and requesting support for biannual overseas travel for medical treatment. When the floor was opened, South Hulhumale Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed to send a letter to the complainant, advising him to raise the matter directly with NSPA. This proposal was seconded by Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir. The proposal was passed unanimously. Details of votes taken in this meeting are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 5th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The first thing that was discussed in today's meeting was the issue regarding the registration of vehicles and policies formulated by the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation regarding vehicle registration. Once the Chairman opened the floor for discussion, two proposals were submitted. 1. As Regulation No 2025/R-34 (6th Amendment to the Motor Vehicle Registration Regulation) partially provides a remedy to the vehicle registration issue, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer proposed to review the issue for later date. (The motion did not proceed to a vote as it did not receive any support from other members.) 2. As Regulation No 2025/R-34 (6th Amendment to the Motor Vehicle Registration Regulation) partially provides a remedy to the vehicle registration issue, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed to close the issue submitted to the Committee. This proposal was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The proposal was passed unanimously. Next, the Committee discussed an issue that raised concerns regarding overtime payment policies and emphasized the need to conduct a human resource audit to address these matters. The issue also highlighted concerns about the quality of healthcare service providers and the importance of identifying systemic issues within the healthcare system to provide effective solutions to these problems. After discussion, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer proposed to send a letter to the relevant institutions to obtain information regarding the matter. This proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. The proposal was passed unanimously. Lastly, the committee proceeded to issue submitted concerning hazardous incidents occurring in areas frequented by tourists, particularly in protected marine parks, as well as the lack of monitoring in the South Ari Protected Area (SAMPA). After deliberation, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed sending a response letter to the member who raised the issue, based on information obtained from the Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Environment. This proposal was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The proposal was passed unanimously. ﻿ Details of votes taken in this meeting are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 4th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The first thing that was discussed in today's meeting was issue referred to the committee by the Union for Employment Agencies of the Maldives raising their concerns regarding Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology’s decision to handover ‘Expat System’ to a Malaysian company and to start providing service through a new system in February 2025. Since the issue is relate to the implementation of policies relating to employment of expatriates in the Maldives under The Employment Act (Law no. 2/2008), it falls under the mandate of Committee on National Security Services. It was clarified to the committee that Article 121 (h) of the Standing Order restricts other committees from investigating matters under the purview of the Committee on National Security Services. After much deliberation among the committee members, South Hulhumale' Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed to seek the advice of the Counsel General of the Parliament to determine whether the issue can be addressed within the Committee’s mandate. The proposal was seconded by South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain. The proposal was passed unanimously. ﻿ Next, the committee discussed the issue regarding the registration of vehicles and policies formulated by the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation regarding vehicle registration. The Committee came to an end without deciding anything regarding this matter.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The first thing that was discussed in today's meeting was the abolition of the Ministry of Housing, Land and Urban Development, renaming the 'Ministry of Construction and Infrastructure' as 'Ministry of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure', renaming the ‘Ministry of Finance’ as 'Ministry of Finance and Planning', abolition of 'Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy' and renaming the 'Ministry of Tourism' as 'Ministry of Tourism and Environment', changing the mandate of Ministry of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure, Ministry of Finance and Planning and Ministry of Tourism and Environment in accordance with the President’s recommendation. Once the Chairman opened the floor, Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed proposed to approve the mandate changes to the 3 ministries in accordance with the President’s recommendation. It was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The proposal was passed unanimously. The committee then proceeded to attend to the issue submitted by North Galolhu Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim regarding the difficulties faced by the MBBS students getting internship opportunities from IGMH. After discussing the responses received from the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazad proposed to meet with the relevant officials of the Ministry of Higher Education, Ministry of Health and IGMH to further review the issue. This proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. The proposal was passed unanimously. Next, the committee discussed the issue submitted by South Hulhumale Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed regarding the registration of vehicles and policies formulated by the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation regarding vehicle registration. The Ministry’s response regarding this issue was shared with the committee. However, as it was time for the voting on the Majlis floor, it was decided to put the matter on the agenda for another day and the meeting ended.

meetings.summary: Today the committee reviewed the approval requests from the President for the appointed ministers to the cabinet on 26 th December 2024, as per article 129 (a) of the constitution. Once the Chairman opened the floor for members, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to approve the 4 ministers appointed by the President as the “Qualifications of Ministers” stated in article 130 of the Constitution of Maldives were fulfilled and none of the cabinet ministers has violated any of the “Restrictions” stated in article 136 of the constitution. And it was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. Then, the members present in the meeting unanimously passed the proposal to give approval for the 4 ministers appointed by the President on 26 th December 2024. After that, when the floor was opened for any issue that the members want to raise, South Hulhumale' Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed to summon Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation to clarify about the registration of vehicles and the policies formulated under the mandate of the Ministry. This proposal was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. Then, the members present in the meeting unanimously passed the proposal to meet the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation to clarify about the registration of vehicles and the policies formulated under the mandate of the Ministry.

meetings.title: 7th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The committee met with the Maldives Hajj cooperation and the Ministry of Islamic Affairs to clarify and discuss the procedure followed in sending Pilgrims to Hajj in the Maldives. They also discussed on how the cooperation utilizes their Hajj quota, their efforts to reduce the price taken for the service of sending pilgrims to Hajj and their efforts to make Hajj cooperation a company that is self-sufficient and profitable. They also discussed main challenges faced by the cooperation and current efforts to further improve the services provided by the cooperation.

meetings.title: 5th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: Today, the first item on the agenda was to discuss the matter sent by the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives (HRCM) regarding the Labor Relations Authority (LRA), stating that the LRA did not share information on employment related cases and does not cooperate with them. Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad noted that it is clear from the information shared by the HRCM (as per the committee’s request for an update) that the challenges mentioned in that complaint was based on cases submitted in the year 2020 and 2021, and since then the management of the LRA has been changed; they are now under Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology. And currently they do share information on such cases. So, he proposed to conclude the issue and file it. It was seconded by Dhangethi Constituency Member Abdulla Rasheed and was passed unanimously The Second item on the agenda was to discuss an issue sent by an individual stating he did not get the opportunity to attend the 2024 Hajj pilgrimage despite making the full payment to the Hajj corporation in the year 2019. Yet, some individuals in his island who made the payment in the year 2023 to the Hajj corporation were able to attend the 2024 Hajj. Once the chairman opened the floor for discussions based on the information received from the Hajj corporation and the Ministry of Islamic affairs, since this is a concerning issue for the people, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed proposed to meet with the Ministry of Islamic Affairs and Hajj corporation to clarify Hajj-related matters. It was seconded by South Hulhumale' Constituency Member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed and was passed unanimously. And regarding the same issue, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to reply to the complainant who sent the issue based on the information received from the Ministry of Islamic Affairs and Hajj corporation. It was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim and was passed unanimously.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: Today as a first item on the agenda, the committee discussed the matter of approving the mandate changes to the Ministry of Gender, family and social services sent by the president as per article 116 (a) of the constitution. Once the chair opened the floor, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to consider the matter outdated and to file it, noting that it was sent by the previous administration and the incumbent president had already sent the newly formed ministries based on their policies along with the mandate changes to the parliament for approval. It was seconded by Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer. The voting details are as follows. Vote: To consider that the mandate changes for the ministry of Gender, family and social services is an outdated issue and to file the case issue. Total no. of members: 11 No. of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 8 Voted No: 0 Abstain: 0 Total Voted: 8 No. of votes required to Pass: 5 Vote Result: Members present in the meeting unanimously passed the proposal. (Members voted in favour: West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhangethi Constituency Member Abdulla Rasheed, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir, and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad Hence, Members present in the meeting unanimously decided to consider that the mandate changes for the ministry of Gender, family and social services is an outdated issue and to file as such. As the second item on the agenda, the committee reviewed the approval requests from the president for the new ministries and their mandates created on 17 th November 2023, as per article 116 (a) of the constitution and the mandate change for three individual ministries on 4 th January 2024, with the changes. The Chair opened the floor for members. Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to approve the matter as sent by the government and it was seconded by West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim. The voting details are as follows. Vote: To approve the ministries created on 17 th November and the mandate changes brought to 3 ministries on 4 th January as sent by the government. Total no. of members: 11 No. of members present: 8 Voted Yes: 6 Voted No: 1 Abstain: 0 Total Voted: 7 No. of votes required to Pass: 4 Vote Result: Majority of the members present in the meeting passed the proposal. (Members voted in favour : West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhangethi Constituency Member Abdulla Rasheed and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad (Members voted against : South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym Hence, the majority of the members present in the committee decided to approve the new ministries created on 17 th November 2023 and the mandate changes of three ministries sent with their changes sent by the president under the discretion given in the article 116 (a) of the constitution. As the fourth item on the agenda, under miscellaneous, the committee discussed on the issue sent by the Human rights commission of the Maldives, regarding the labor relations authority for not sharing the requested information and lack of support. Since this issue was sent to two committees of the parliament (government oversight committee and Human rights and Gender committee), the committee decided to clarify if the Human rights and Gender committee has done any work, before proceeding any further. As the fifth item on the agenda, the committee discussed the issue of delays in Faadhihpolhu state house building renovation submitted by Lh. Atoll council. Once the chair opened the floor for members, Felidhoo Constituency Member Adam Zahir proposed to send the issue letter to the Committee on Decentralization. meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The first item on today’s agenda is to set the working quorum and the voting quorum of the Committee. The Standing Order states that the working quorum of a committee shall not be lower than 1/3 of its members. When the chair opened the floor for members, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad, proposed the working quorum of the Committee as 4 members and the voting quorum of the committee as 6 members; it was seconded by South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym. Below are the voting details of the proposal. Vote: Committee Working Quorum as 4 members and Committee Voting Quorum as 6 members. Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 8 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 8 Required to Pass: 5 Result: Passed (Members voted in favour South Hulhumale’ Constituency Memeber Dr. Ahmed Shamheed, West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhaandhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Fazeel and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad. Hence, the committee unanimously passed 4 members as the working quorum and 6 members as the voting quorum. Secondly, the committee discussed the working quorum for the summoned meetings stipulated in section 163 of the standing order of 19 th Majlis. Dhaandhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Fazeel proposed as 6 members as working quorum for the summoned meetings mentioned under article 163 of the standing order of 19 th Majlis; it was seconded by Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer. Below are the voting details of the proposal. Vote: Working quorum for the summoned meetings as 6 members. Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 8 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 8 Required to Pass: 5 Result: Passed (Members voted in favour: South Hulhumale’ Constituency Memeber Dr. Ahmed Shamheed, West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhaandhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Fazeel and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad. Hence, the members present in the meeting unanimously passed the working quorum for the summoned meetings as 6 members. Thirdly, the committee worked on the administrative procedure for approving the cabinet members appointed by the president as stipulated in the article 129 (a) of the constitution and a procedure for other issues that does not fall under the article 151 of the Standing Order of 19th Majlis. Once the chair opened the floor for members, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to adopt the same policies used by the Government Oversight Committee of the 19 th Majlis, without any changes. West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim seconded the proposal. Below are the voting details of the proposal. Vote: Adopt the same policies used by the Government Oversight Committee of the 19 th Majlis, without any changes. Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 8 Voted against: 0 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 8 Required to Pass: 5 Result: Passed (Members voted in favour: South Hulhumale’ Constituency Memeber Dr. Ahmed Shamheed, West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhaandhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Fazeel and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad Hence, the members present in the meeting unanimously decided to adopt the same policies used by the Government Oversight Committee of the 19th Majlis, without any changes. As the 5 th item on the agenda, the committee discussed preparing a work plan as stipulated in article 148 of the Standing Order of 19th Majlis. The Committee discussed the matter and decided that the committee secretariat will prepare and submit a work plan by 30 th June 2024. The committee reviewed the issue on the approval of three cabinet ministers appointed by the President on Monday (29 th January 2024), as the last item on today’s agenda. Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad proposed to approve the three names, as the requirements stated in article 130 of the constitution “qualification of Ministers” were fulfilled and none of the cabinet ministers has violated article 136 of the constitution. “Restrictions” Article 136 states, (a) A member of the Cabinet shall not hold any other public office or office of profit, actively engage in a business or in the practice of any profession, or any other income generating employment, be employed by any person, buy or lease any property belonging to the State, or have a financial interest in any transaction between the State and another party. (b) A member of the Cabinet shall not use his position or any information entrusted to him by virtue of his office to improperly benefit himself or any other person. This proposal was seconded by Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. Below are the voting details of the proposal. Vote: Approve the three cabinet members appointed by the president Total number of members: 11 Number of members present: 9 Voted Yes: 7 Voted against: 1 Abstain: 0 Total voted: 8 Required to Pass: 5 Result: Passed (Members voted in favour: South Hulhumale’ Constituency Memeber Dr. Ahmed Shamheed, West Henveyru Constituency Member Ali Ibrahim, South Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Musthafa Hussain, Ihavandhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Naseer, Dhidhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed, Dhaandhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Fazeel and Central Fuvahmulah Constituency Member Ali Fazaad (Members voted against: South Galolhu Constituency Member Meekail Ahmed Nasym Hence, the majority of the members present in the Committee meeting voted in favor of approving the three members appointed to the cabinet. The committee postponed the rest of the matter on the agenda to another meeting and ended today’s meeting.
